statements.title: Statement Studio
statements.intro: UCAS personal statement (three structured questions from 2026 entry). Structured guidance plus character / format self-checks to help you write a strong PS yourself.
statements.aiNotice: This tool assists; it does not ghost-write. AI feedback requires sign-in and separate data-processing consent. It is for practice only, may be unavailable or inaccurate, and is not human or official assessment.

questions.title: Q1 · Why do you want to study this course?
questions.hint: Explain where your interest and motivation come from; avoid vague 'always loved it' — back it with specific experiences.

questions.title: Q2 · How have your studies prepared you?
questions.hint: Connect your A-Level subjects, topics, reading or projects, and how they built relevant knowledge and skills.

questions.title: Q3 · What have you done outside education, and why is it useful?
questions.hint: Competitions, research, internships, volunteering, self-study — focus on what you learned and its relevance.

selfCheck: Original work, not copied or ghost-written (UCAS runs similarity detection)
Focus on academic motivation and ability, not unrelated personal sentiment
Use concrete examples and outcomes, not vague adjectives
Avoid clichéd openings (famous quotes, dictionary definitions)

timeline.title: Application Timeline
timeline.disclaimer: Dates reflect a typical application cycle; verify with each university. To change your intake year, visit

early.label: Well ahead
early.desc: Plenty of time before the main deadlines — ideal for deep university research and drafting a polished statement.

on-track.label: On track
on-track.desc: Following the milestones steadily — focus on personal statement quality and complete documentation.

late.label: Time is tight
late.desc: Deadlines are close — prioritise getting core materials submitted before any further optimisation.

research.title: Research universities & courses
research.desc: Identify target universities and courses; gather entry requirements, tuition, and rankings.
research.earlyTip: Ahead of schedule: read course syllabuses in depth and prepare specific questions for open days.
research.lateTip: Time limited: focus on 5–8 schools you already have in mind and gather their key requirements quickly.

ucasReg.title: Register a UCAS account
ucasReg.desc: Create an account on the UCAS website, fill in your basic details, and prepare to start your application.
ucasReg.lateTip: Register now — account activation takes time; don't leave it until the final week.

oxbridge.title: Oxbridge deadline (15 Oct)
oxbridge.desc: UCAS applications for Oxford or Cambridge must be submitted by this date.
oxbridge.earlyTip: If Oxbridge is on your list, start preparing admissions tests (MAT/STEP/TSA etc.) now.
oxbridge.lateTip: If you're applying to Oxbridge your personal statement must be finalised immediately — no delay.

psDraft.title: Personal statement first draft
psDraft.desc: Complete a first draft of your UCAS personal statement (3 structured questions) to allow revision time.
psDraft.earlyTip: Write multiple versions to compare, or ask a teacher or peer for early feedback.
psDraft.lateTip: Go straight to a final draft — make sure the structure is complete before polishing wording.

hkOpen.title: HK applications open
hkOpen.desc: HKU, HKUST and other universities typically open direct-admission portals from November — watch official websites.

ucasMain.title: UCAS main deadline (15 Jan)
ucasMain.desc: Deadline for all non-Oxbridge UK UCAS choices; all five choices must be submitted by this date.
ucasMain.earlyTip: Submitting early is possible — some universities review on a rolling basis.
ucasMain.lateTip: Under two months to go — lock in your personal statement and references now, no margin for delay.

hkDeadline.title: HK direct-admission deadline
hkDeadline.desc: Most HK universities close direct admission between March and April — confirm each school's own date.

ucasDecisions.title: UCAS decisions arriving
ucasDecisions.desc: Offers and rejections will appear in UCAS Track — keep notifications on.

ucasReply.title: UCAS reply deadline
ucasReply.desc: Choose your Firm and Insurance universities in UCAS before the reply deadline.

exams.title: A-Level exam season
exams.desc: May–June A-Level exams determine whether you meet the conditions of any conditional offer.
exams.earlyTip: Well prepared — maintain momentum and practise past papers to optimise timing.
exams.lateTip: Intensive revision: focus on high-frequency topics and ensure core content is solid.

results.title: Results day & confirmation
results.desc: Grades released; conditional offers confirmed. If grades fall short, Clearing opens immediately.
